title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III will miss game vs. Falcons with groin injury
content:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will not play in Sunday’s road game against the Atlanta Falcons because of a groin injury, the team announced Saturday.

Walker, second in the NFL in rushing with 872 yards, will be missing his first game with the Chiefs.

The injury showed up suddenly. Walker, who was a full participant in Wednesday and Thursday’s practices, was held out of Friday’s drills, Chiefs coach Andy Reid announced.

“Came in this morning and had a tight groin, so we just sat him out of practice today,” Reid said Friday. “We’ll just see how he feels.”

Walker’s absence spoils what would’ve been a primetime running-back matchup between the NFL’s top rushers. The Falcons’ Bijan Robinson, who has played in one more game than Walker, leads the league with 880 rushing yards.

This should also be the first extended look at Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson. A 2026 fifth-round pick, Johnson has impressed in limited action while primarily used as a third-down back, contributing 14 catches for 237 yards while showing strong elusiveness. Per Pro Football Focus, Johnson’s 11 missed tackles forced as a receiver rank as the seventh-best mark in the NFL despite his low catch total.

Chiefs third-string running back Jaydn Ott is also listed as questionable for Sunday with a groin injury. Practice squad running back Nate Carter is the only other true running back available on the active roster.
